claim: A small number of animal long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have known effects on cellular processes examined in vitro.
source: Although a small number of the vast array of animal long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have known effects on cellular processes examined in vitro, the extent of their contributions to normal cell processes throughout development, differentiation and disease for the most part remains less clear.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract, representing the current state of the field.

claim: The extent of lncRNA contributions to normal cell processes throughout development, differentiation and disease remains unclear.
source: Although a small number of the vast array of animal long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have known effects on cellular processes examined in vitro, the extent of their contributions to normal cell processes throughout development, differentiation and disease for the most part remains less clear.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the field based on the current state of research.

claim: Phenotypes arising from deletion of an entire genomic locus cannot be unequivocally attributed to the loss of the lncRNA per se.
source: Phenotypes arising from deletion of an entire genomic locus cannot be unequivocally attributed either to the loss of the lncRNA per se or to the associated loss of other overlapping DNA regulatory elements.

claim: Phenotypes arising from deletion of an entire genomic locus cannot be unequivocally attributed to the associated loss of other overlapping DNA regulatory elements.

claim: Antisense oligonucleotides are able to bind to nascent RNA transcripts and trigger RNase H mediated degradation of the transcript in the nucleus.
source: Antisense oligonucleotides are able to bind to nascent RNA transcripts and trigger RNase H mediated degradation of the transcript in the nucleus.

claim: The extent to which exclusively nuclear lncRNAs can be knocked down by RNAi remains unclear.

claim: Changes in DNA methylation at the Evf-2 enhancer can be rescued by Evf-2 expression from a separate transgene.
source: Importantly these changes can be rescued by Evf-2 expression from a separate transgene, implying that they are dependent on the lncRNA itself (Berghoff et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Berghoff et al., 2013.

claim: Knockdown of lincRNA-p21 by RNAi originally suggested a trans-acting mechanism, in which the lncRNA was involved in recruiting protein complexes to chromatin.
source: Similarly to this example, knockdown of lincRNA-p21 by RNAi originally suggested a trans-acting mechanism, in which the lncRNA was involved in recruiting protein complexes to chromatin (Huarte et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Huarte et al., 2010.

claim: Subsequent studies where the promoter of lincRNA-p21 was deleted or its transcription was blocked by antisense oligonucleotides have highlighted a different role, as this lncRNA regulates the adjacent p21 gene in cis, without having trans-acting effects.
source: Nevertheless, subsequent studies where the promoter of the lncRNA was deleted or its transcription was blocked by antisense oligonucleotides have highlighted a different role, as this lncRNA regulates the adjacent p21 gene in cis, without having trans-acting effects (Dimitrova et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dimitrova et al., 2014.

claim: The two sets of differentially expressed genes from RNAi and promoter deletion/antisense oligonucleotide studies of lincRNA-p21 did not overlap significantly.
source: Whilst both studies analysed by RNAseq the effect of lncRNA depletion on global gene expression in mouse embryonic fibroblasts, the two sets of differentially expressed genes did not overlap significantly.
evidence: This is data comparing the two studies.

claim: When analysing lncRNA function, it is important to consider multiple loss-of-function strategies that address multiple mechanisms of action.
source: When analysing lncRNA function, it is thus important to consider multiple loss-of-function strategies that address multiple mechanisms of action.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on inference from the discrepancies observed in different studies.

claim: The Drosophila bxd lncRNA is expressed from within the HOX cluster, adjacent to the Ultrabithorax (Ubx) gene.
source: The potential confounding effects of techniques used to separate DNA- from RNA-dependent function are further exemplified by studies of the Drosophila bxd lncRNA, which is expressed from within the HOX cluster, adjacent to the Ultrabithorax (Ubx) gene.
evidence: This is stated as a factual observation about the genomic location of bxd.

claim: The expression of bxd is highly specific and occurs in the same broad region of the embryo as the Ubx gene, although notably never within the same cell.
source: Its expression is highly specific and occurs in the same broad region of the embryo as the Ubx gene, although notably never within the same cell (Petruk et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Petruk et al., 2006.

claim: Studies of bxd loss-of-function using different techniques have yielded conflicting interpretations.
source: Studies of bxd loss-of-function using different techniques have yielded conflicting interpretations.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the literature on bxd.

claim: Small deletions within bxd lncRNA cause dramatic effects on expression of the neighbouring Ubx gene.
source: It has long been known that small deletions within this lncRNA cause dramatic effects on expression of the neighbouring Ubx gene (Lewis, 1978), resulting in homoeotic transformations.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lewis, 1978.

claim: Small deletions within bxd lncRNA result in homoeotic transformations.
source: It has long been known that small deletions within this lncRNA cause dramatic effects on expression of the neighbouring Ubx gene (Lewis, 1978), resulting in homoeotic transformations.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lewis, 1978.

claim: Certain allelic combinations of bxd deletions are able to generate a four-winged fly.
source: Indeed, certain allelic combinations are able to generate a four-winged fly.
evidence: This is stated as a known phenotype from bxd deletions.

claim: The act of transcription of bxd lncRNA represses Ubx in cis by altering protein binding to the Ubx promoter.
source: More recent studies of the same deletions suggest that the act of transcription of this lncRNA represses Ubx in cis by altering protein binding to the Ubx promoter (Petruk et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Petruk et al., 2006.

claim: Inversion of the bxd promoter, driving transcription in the wrong direction whilst maintaining genomic composition, results in very minor effects on Ubx expression, and then only later in development.
source: In contrast, it was reported that inversion of the bxd promoter, driving transcription in the wrong direction whilst maintaining genomic composition, results in very minor effects on Ubx expression, and then only later in development (Pease et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pease et al., 2013.

claim: A deletion removing the bxd promoter induced a Cdx-like gain of function of Ubx.
source: Also, a deletion removing the promoter induced a Cdx-like gain of function of Ubx (Sipos et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sipos et al., 2007.

claim: Correct interpretation of loss-of-function experiments at complex loci requires careful consideration of potentially confounding factors.
source: Clearly, correct interpretation of such loss-of-function experiments, at such complex loci, requires careful consideration of potentially confounding factors.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological principle based on the bxd example.

claim: Contrasting results of different experiments may arise because of a lncRNA's involvement in different mechanisms in different cellular contexts.
source: Contrasting results of different experiments may also arise because of a lncRNA's involvement in different mechanisms in different cellular contexts.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about potential explanations for discrepancies.

claim: In embryonic cells, transcription of Airn silences the adjacent Igf2r gene.
source: For example, in embryonic cells, transcription of Airn silences the adjacent Igf2r gene (Latos et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Latos et al., 2012.

claim: In extraembryonic tissues, Airn acts more distally by recruiting the histone methyltransferase G9a to imprinted genes.
source: whereas in extraembryonic tissues it acts more distally by recruiting the histone methyltransferase G9a to imprinted genes (Nagano et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nagano et al., 2008.

claim: The study of lncRNAs is still in its infancy.
source: The study of lncRNAs is still in its infancy
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of the current state of the field.

claim: The biochemical and genetic techniques used to address the significance and mechanisms of action of lncRNAs have only recently been developed or adapted from those used for investigating protein-coding genes.
source: and the biochemical and genetic techniques used to address the true significance and mechanisms of action of this class of RNA have only recently been developed or adapted from those used for investigating protein-coding genes.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of the current state of the field.

claim: Techniques for studying lncRNAs must be used with caution and with appropriate controls.
source: Such techniques must therefore be used with caution and with appropriate controls (Brockdorff, 2013; Riley and Steitz, 2013).
evidence: This is a recommendation supported by citations to Brockdorff, 2013 and Riley and Steitz, 2013.

claim: The optimal strategy to study a lncRNA's loss of function depends on the mechanism by which it acts, in particular in a cis or trans configuration.
source: From the examples described above, it is apparent that the optimal strategy with which to study a lncRNA's loss of function depends both on the mechanism by which it acts, in particular in a cis or trans configuration, and the regulatory sequences present within its locus.
evidence: This is an inference based on the examples discussed in the manuscript.

claim: The optimal strategy to study a lncRNA's loss of function depends on the regulatory sequences present within its locus.
source: From the examples described above, it is apparent that the optimal strategy with which to study a lncRNA's loss of function depends both on the mechanism by which it acts, in particular in a cis or trans configuration, and the regulatory sequences present within its locus.
evidence: This is an inference based on the examples discussed in the manuscript.

claim: Early lessons learnt from paradigm repressor lncRNAs, such as Xist, and imprinted lncRNAs such as Airn or Kcnq1ot1, should guide the design of experiments on more recently identified lncRNAs.
source: We suggest that early lessons learnt from paradigm repressor lncRNAs, such as Xist, and imprinted lncRNAs such as Airn or Kcnq1ot1, should guide the design of experiments on more recently identified lncRNAs.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on inference from established lncRNA examples.

claim: Introduction of multiple alleles necessary to adequately dissect lncRNA in vivo function will be greatly aided by recent advances in genome engineering using designer site-specific nucleases such as CRISPR/Cas9 and TALENs.
source: Introduction of the multiple alleles that will be necessary to adequately dissect lncRNA in vivo function will be greatly aided by recent advances in genome engineering using designer site-specific nucleases such as CRISPR/Cas9 and TALENs.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about how new technologies will facilitate lncRNA research.

claim: The introduction of fast acute loss-of-function systems for lncRNAs would greatly facilitate lncRNA investigation.
source: The introduction of fast acute loss-of-function systems for lncRNAs, for example those that insert a sequence-specific ribonuclease site whose nuclease is under drug inducible control, would also greatly facilitate lncRNA investigation.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about potential future technologies.

claim: The trans function of a lncRNA may be investigated using locus deletion, promoter deletion, inversions, transcriptional termination or RNAi.
source: The trans function of a lncRNA may be investigated using locus deletion, promoter deletion, inversions, transcriptional termination or RNAi.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological recommendation.

claim: Trans-acting lncRNA investigation strategies should be combined with genetic rescue experiments, where the lncRNA is expressed from an independent transgene inserted at a location distinct from the lncRNA locus.
source: Where possible, these strategies should be combined with genetic rescue experiments, where the lncRNA is expressed from an independent transgene inserted at a location distinct from the lncRNA locus.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological recommendation.

claim: Rescue experiments using expression of the lncRNA from an independent transgene separate RNA-dependent effects from those arising from the manipulation of the underlying DNA.
source: This strategy separates RNA-dependent effects from those arising from the manipulation of the underlying DNA.
evidence: This is an inference about the purpose of rescue experiments.

claim: Rescue experiments using expression of the lncRNA from an independent transgene are only possible for trans-acting lncRNAs where the RNA moiety itself and not the act of transcription is critical for function.
source: Rescue experiments using expression of the lncRNA from an independent transgene are only possible for trans-acting lncRNAs where the RNA moiety itself and not the act of transcription is critical for function.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the rescue approach.

claim: The cis function of a lncRNA may be investigated using a combination of several alleles, such as insertion of transcriptional terminators, promoter deletions and inversions.
source: The cis function of a lncRNA may be investigated using a combination of several alleles, such as insertion of transcriptional terminators, promoter deletions and inversions.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological recommendation.

claim: Several alleles are likely to be required to separate lncRNA-dependent from other effects and to reveal artefacts of genetic engineering.
source: Several alleles are likely to be required to separate lncRNA-dependent from other effects and, as controls, to reveal artefacts of genetic engineering.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological recommendation based on inference.

claim: Engineered inversions can be used to separate the lncRNA locus from its potential neighbouring target gene to investigate its roles in cis.
source: Engineered inversions can also be used to separate the lncRNA locus from its potential neighbouring target gene to investigate its roles in cis.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological recommendation.

claim: Use of site-specific recombinases, such as the phiC31/attP system as 'landing sites' or for recombination mediated cassette exchange, will greatly enhance our ability to generate allelic series.
source: Use of site-specific recombinases, such as the phiC31/attP system (Bateman et al., 2006; Zhu et al., 2014) as 'landing sites' or for recombination mediated cassette exchange, will greatly enhance our ability to generate such allelic series.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about how technologies will facilitate research, supported by citations to Bateman et al., 2006 and Zhu et al., 2014.

claim: The lncRNA locus may be deleted and replaced by a recombinase 'landing site' into which different constructs can be introduced to investigate phenotype rescue.
source: For example, the lncRNA locus may be deleted and replaced by a recombinase 'landing site' into which different constructs can be introduced to investigate phenotype rescue.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological recommendation.

claim: If lncRNA biologists are to resolve the true in vivo functions of lncRNAs, then the strengths and weaknesses of available techniques will need to be acknowledged.
source: In summary, if lncRNA biologists are to resolve the true in vivo functions of these numerous and enigmatic transcripts, then the strengths and weaknesses of available techniques will need to be acknowledged.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the discussion.

claim: Resolution of lncRNA function will derive from the careful and comprehensive genetic dissection of individual loci using multiple alleles.
source: Resolution will no doubt derive from the careful and comprehensive genetic dissection of individual loci using multiple alleles.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the discussion.

claim: The field of lncRNA biology would benefit greatly from the development of additional approaches that are effective in distinguishing effects mediated by lncRNAs as molecular species from their effect on gene regulatory elements with which lncRNA loci are interleaved across the mammalian genome.
source: The field of lncRNA biology would benefit greatly from the development of additional approaches that are effective in distinguishing effects mediated by lncRNAs as molecular species from their effect on gene regulatory elements with which lncRNA loci are interleaved across the mammalian genome.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion and recommendation for future research.
